ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening, before signature of any formation document, of every general partner, limited partner holding at least 25% economic or voting rights, authorized signatory, and each natural person UBO against: (i) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; (ii) United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List and Canada's implementing measures under the United Nations Act; (iii) Canadian sanctions regulations promulgated under the Special Economic Measures Act; (iv) FINTRAC-required PEP databases covering current and former domestic and foreign PEPs, including family members and close associates; and (v) RCMP/CSIS watchlists and Canadian Criminal Code listed-entity records. Identity verification evidence must be certified and records retained for at least five years, with re-screening upon the admission of any new partner, any change of control, annual registration renewal, and each new payment rail onboarding event such as Shopify Payments, Stripe, or local point-of-sale acquirers.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: B.C. Corporate Online (CORES) System of the British Columbia Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legal name of a British Columbia limited partnership must be in English or French and must end with the prescribed legal element 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', or 'LP'. Trade names derived from non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet for public registry purposes, and the transliteration must appear distinctive and not confusingly similar to any existing registered name, trademark, or recognizable geographic term in the NUANS database.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the B.C. Registrar of Companies rejects a proposed name, the applicant may within 30 days of receipt of the written refusal submit a Request for Reconsideration to the Registrar, attaching the original name search report, comparing distinguishable elements, and citing any supporting Canadian trademark or trade-name authorities. If the reconsideration is refused, the applicant may either file an alternative name reservation or apply to the Supreme Court of British Columbia for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 241, and any such application should be commenced promptly and in all events no later than six months after the reconsideration decision. A single extension of the name reservation for an additional 56 days may be requested before the initial reservation expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for this industry provided the registered office address is a physical street address within British Columbia attended during ordinary business hours and capable of accepting service of process, and a separate records delivery address in British Columbia maintains the limited partnership's statutory books and records. Postal-only forwarding services are not sufficient to establish statutory presence, and Canada Revenue Agency may disregard a virtual-only address if central management and control is not in fact exercised in British Columbia.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: LOW: probability of an unannounced physical inspection during the pre-incorporation stage is 0%, and the estimated probability within the first 12 months post-registration is below 2% for this standard-risk e-commerce merchandising operation. The B.C. registry does not conduct general premises inspections; Canada Revenue Agency audits are ordinarily predicated on written notice, and unannounced site visits would only be expected following a FINTRAC/RCMP complaint, a Health Canada product-safety matter, or a documented consumer-protection violation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal and Provincial Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – Business Registration Online; BC Ministry of Finance (Provincial Sales Tax Branch)

Register separately for BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) if the partnership will sell taxable goods at retail, and enroll the partnership with WorkSafeBC for mandatory workers' compensation coverage.

Extract of partnership agreement confirming general partner authority
Schedule of partners' addresses and SIN/BN for compliance
Completed CRA RC1W and BC PST application forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: CRA account discrepancies are cured by filing an RC65 Business Information Change form or by requesting a BN revision; PST registration errors are remedied through the BC PST account adjustment portal or by direct rectification with the Ministry of Finance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: VOC emissions ≤ 1.0 t/yr (Metro Vancouver emissions permitting threshold); wastewater BOD ≤ 300 mg/L, TSS ≤ 350 mg/L, pH 6.0-10.0 per Municipal Sewer Bylaw; plastic scrap and waste consolidation and recycling obligations; compliance with the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 (vinyl chloride monomer and paint substance restrictions) and the BC Environmental Management Act (hazardous waste manifesting).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and certification by the local Fire Marshal (Class B flammables storage and spray booth compliance); structural load assessment and certification for production racks, rotocasting ovens and material handling equipment; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety clearance (industrial hygiene, ventilation, and personal protective equipment); municipal zoning and occupancy verification for an industrial producer on the target premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada — federal GST/HST, income tax, payroll and customs program accounts (Business Registration Online at canada.ca; My Business Account portal). Provincial Sales Tax (PST) in British Columbia is separately administered by the BC Ministry of Finance, Consumer Taxation Branch through eTaxBC (etax.gov.bc.ca), with PST registration via Form FIN 419. Business registry: BC Registry Services (Corporate Online) under the Partnership Act, RSBC 1996, c. 348.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Obtain a 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN) for the BC limited partnership by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number and Certain Program Accounts) with the Sudbury Tax Centre or online via Business Registration Online (BRO); non-resident applicants must appoint a Canadian representative/agent authorized under Form RC59 and provide a Canadian address for service. Step 2: Add the GST/HST program account (RT suffix) once worldwide taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 in any single calendar quarter or in the last four consecutive calendar quarters; a non-resident below the threshold may voluntarily register to claim Input Tax Credits and must designate a resident agent for CRA notices. Step 3: Register the LP for BC PST at the Consumer Taxation Branch via eTaxBC once gross revenue from BC taxable sales exceeds CAD 10,000 in any month or CAD 50,000 in any 12 consecutive months, obtaining a 9-digit BC PST vendor number. Step 4: Register the limited partnership with BC Registry Services by filing the Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form LP-1) and file the annual report; an extra-provincial or foreign LP carrying on business in BC must also extra-provincially register. Step 5: Add the CRA Import/Export program account (RM suffix) for customs purposes; for exports, report through CBSA using the Canadian Export Declaration (B13A) or carrier-submitted ACI eManifest data. The general partner manages all fiscal registrations; partners are not separately registered for the partnership's GST/PST.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — A BC limited partnership is fiscally transparent for Canadian income tax: the LP computes income under Part I of the Income Tax Act but does not pay income tax itself; each partner (individual, corporation, or non-resident) is allocated a share of partnership income/loss and taxed at partner level. The LP has territorial Canadian-source scope through its Canadian permanent establishment; non-resident partners are subject to Part XIII gross-base withholding (25% or treaty-reduced) on allocated Canadian-source business income unless protected by treaty or a net-basis election. Distinct from income tax, the LP is a separate deemed person for GST/HST under ETA subsection 272.1 and a mandatory 'vendor' for BC PST; the LP's tax-exempt-zone status does not apply (no free-zone benefits for toys manufactured in BC).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no general check-the-box election; entity classification is statutory. Relevant mechanisms: (i) Income Tax Act subsection 216(1) election — a non-resident partner with Canadian-source rental or real-property income from the partnership may file a net-basis Part I return instead of Part XIII gross withholding; (ii) ITA subsection 102(1)/102(2) — the partnership is a 'Canadian partnership' only if all partners are Canadian-resident; the presence of foreign partners makes it a non-Canadian partnership, triggering Part XIII compliance and s. 216 eligibility; (iii) ETA subsection 211(1) voluntary registration election — a small supplier may elect to register for GST/HST early to recover ITCs on pre-registration inputs; (iv) hybrid mismatch timing election under ITA subsection 18.2(13) and ETA section 272.1 — where a US partner classifies the Canadian LP as an association taxable as a corporation under US Treas. Reg. §301.7701-3 (check-the-box), the LP is a reverse hybrid; Canada's hybrid mismatch rules (ITA ss. 18.2/18.3, effective for later taxation years) automatically deny deductions, and the election may only align timing where the mismatch is eliminated; (v) ETA subsection 273(1) joint election to make zero-rated exports taxable — available but commercially inadvisable for an export manufacturer and should not be executed; and (vi) for BC PST, no elective regimes exist; vendor registration and PST collection are mandatory once thresholds are met.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST (federal value-added tax) combined with British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST), a retail sales-and-use tax. British Columbia is a non-participating (non-HST) province, so only the 5% federal GST applies at the federal level, plus the separate 7% BC PST on retail supplies of designer blind-box toys to BC consumers, for a combined 12% consumer tax burden.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST: CAD 30,000 in taxable worldwide supplies in a single calendar quarter or over the last four consecutive calendar quarters (small-supplier threshold); registration is mandatory above the threshold for a person carrying on business in Canada, and voluntary below it. BC PST: CAD 10,000 in gross revenue from taxable sales in BC in a single month, or CAD 50,000 over the immediately preceding 12 consecutive months. Both thresholds apply to the BC LP in its own capacity as GST registrant and PST vendor; the LP must also file annual BC registry reports, but no separate BC income-tax registration is required for the partnership entity itself.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, government pre-validation, e-invoice digital stamping, or continuous transaction control regime. E-invoicing is voluntary under the Pan-Canadian Peppol framework (PEPPOL BIS 3.0 through the CRA-accredited Canadian e-invoicing Service Provider network). Mandatory compliance is limited to: (i) invoice content under ETA subsection 221(1) and section 223 — seller's name/trading name, GST/HST registration number, invoice date, taxable amount, tax rate and tax amount, and buyer name/address for supplies over CAD 1,500; (ii) separate disclosure of the 5% GST and 7% BC PST on every invoice/receipt under BC PSTA record-keeping rules; (iii) electronic filing of GST/HST returns (Form GST34) via GST/HST NETFILE or My Business Account on monthly, quarterly, or annual cycles; and (iv) electronic filing of BC PST returns via eTaxBC on the assigned filing frequency; Shopify Payments and Stripe must be configured to apply the correct BC PST code for retail tangible personal property and the 5% GST at the point of sale, with no API-based fiscal clearance required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: Supplies of designer blind-box toys are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V (sections 1-5) where the supplier exports the goods and delivers them to a destination outside Canada; export must occur 'as soon after' the supply as is reasonable (CRA administrative guidance: generally within 60 days), and the supplier must retain prescribed export evidence per GST/HST Memorandum 4-3. Goods shipped to a Canadian address (e.g., a third-party logistics warehouse in Richmond, BC for domestic fulfilment) are not zero-rated. Services and IP: design, prototyping, rotocasting/moulding, marketing, and licensing/royalty services supplied to a non-resident not registered for GST/HST are zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, sections 7 and 10, provided the supply is not in respect of real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada; the BC LP should confirm the GST/HST status of each foreign licensee in its style-guide and character-IP licensing agreements. Export sales generate input tax credit refunds through the normal GST/HST net-tax calculation; no separate VAT refund mechanism is required for a registered exporter.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Canadian Export Declaration (B13A) or, for low-value courier shipments under CAD 2,000, the Courier Low-Value Shipment (CLVS) commercial-invoice data, showing the CRA RM/BN number, export date, HS heading 9503 (toys), destination country, and declared value.

Transport document evidencing departure from Canada and foreign delivery: ocean Bill of Lading or Sea Waybill, Air Waybill (AWB), cross-border truck manifest/CMR, or courier waybill bearing the foreign consignee's name and address.

Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent payment evidence: SWIFT MT103 wire confirmation, PayPal/Stripe settlement report, or buyer's purchase order matched with bank receipt, evidencing foreign-currency settlement and the CAD equivalent used on the export invoice.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA audits export zero-rating claims under GST/HST Memorandum 4-3 by demanding the export declaration, transport document, and payment/remittance evidence within 30 days of a written request; failure to substantiate reverses the zero-rating, reassesses GST, claws back any ITC refunds with interest from the original refund date, and may trigger penalties. Legal consequences include: (i) gross negligence penalty of 50% of the tax sought to be evaded or refund improperly obtained (ETA section 285); (ii) failure-to-file and failure-to-remit penalties (ETA section 280) of 6% plus 2% per complete month of arrears, with compound daily interest at CRA's prescribed rate; (iii) criminal prosecution under ETA section 327 and Income Tax Act section 239 with fines up to CAD 200,000 and/or up to two years imprisonment; (iv) deregistration and public disclosure for wilful misrepresentation; and (v) joint and several liability of the general partner — and, per CRA administrative position, limited partners — for the partnership's GST/PST debts under ETA subsection 272.1(3) and the BC Provincial Sales Tax Act. Canada imposes no statutory 180-day FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day figure is a contractual and bank-compliance benchmark only, while the ETA requires export within a 'reasonable time' (60-day CRA administrative guide) and non-resident partner distributions remain separately subject to Part XIII withholding and treaty reporting.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) acts as the monetary authority, but Canada maintains no dedicated centralized exchange-control administration. Foreign exchange prudential oversight is embedded in the Bank Act, the Canadian Payments Act, and Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) guidance for authorised Schedule I banks. FINTRAC administers cross-border currency reporting and suspicious transaction monitoring, while the Investment Canada Act addresses non-resident investment review, not exchange controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible under a floating exchange-rate regime. Canada imposes no material exchange controls on current-account or capital-account transactions; profit remittance by way of non-resident dividends, partnership distributions, or head-office charges is not exchange-controlled. Non-resident withholding tax under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act (Canada) may apply and be reduced by an applicable income tax treaty, but this is a tax compliance matter rather than a currency restriction. There is no requirement to obtain a central-bank permit for capital contributions, trade settlements, or hedging payments.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada has no mandatory surrender rule for export proceeds. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency in a Canadian bank account or converted at a Canadian bank at commercial rates; there is no statutory timeline for repatriation and no conversion ratio. FINTRAC requires a cross-border currency and monetary instrument report for physical cash movements exceeding CAD 10,000 or its foreign-exchange equivalent. For Canadian tax and accounting purposes, export revenue must be converted to Canadian dollars using the Bank of Canada noon exchange rate or a consistent acceptable rate under IFRS, but this is a tax recognition requirement, not a surrender obligation.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium as a payment facilitation layer, Low as a replacement for a regulated Canadian bank account. Offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) are not banks under Canadian law and cannot directly hold settlement accounts in Canadian Payments Canada systems. An offshore EMI may function only as a payment gateway if it enters into a sponsoring-bank arrangement with a Canadian chartered bank and, where applicable, registers as a money services business or payment service provider with FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Such accounts also do not carry Canada Deposit Insurance Corporation (CDIC) coverage, and downstream vendors may reject settlement from unregulated digital EMIs; therefore the CA_LP treasury policy should treat EMI rails as secondary, never as the sole clearing channel.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian AML/KYC rules do not impose an absolute physical-branch interview. Under PCMLTFA, financial institutions may verify identity remotely using the prescribed non-face-to-face method, including dual-source identity verification through an approved credit bureau or notarised document package. In BC practice, Schedule I banks nonetheless often require at least one general partner, senior authorised signatory, or BC-resident operator to complete a live video interview with corporate compliance; this is heightened where the limited partnership has non-resident partners. The CA_LP must register as an extraprovincial limited partnership in BC, appoint a BC representative/attorney for service if no BC-resident directors exist, and provide a certified register of partners, because the bank will treat absence of BC nexus as a KYC red flag.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners holding significant influence or unusual beneficial-ownership concentration in the limited partnership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete beneficial-ownership waterfall identified through the limited partnership agreement, trust declarations, corporate registry extracts, passports of all natural-person owners, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements, six-month bank statements of each material partner, organisational chart demonstrating economic substance, and confirmation that no bearer shares or nominee chains exist.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce designer-toy model producing high-volume, low-value cross-border merchant settlements into a BC account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan, Shopify/Stripe merchant statements, platform payout reconciliation reports, product catalogue and wholesale/retail pricing, customs and HS classification (ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339930), supplier contracts, third-party logistics bill-of-lading and freight-forwarder invoices, and a compliance memorandum showing that payment flows arise from the sale of physical toys, not from unlicensed remittance or money-service activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payment destinations involving Asia-Pacific manufacturing counterparties or USD concentration triggering enhanced transaction monitoring
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed vendor purchase orders, settlement invoices, shipping documents, confirmed letters of credit, customs entry summaries, foreign-exchange forward cover documentation, sanctions and PEP screening of all counterparties, and six months of projected transaction volumes with evidence of genuine commercial trade and no obligations to act as an intermediary for third-party funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Proposed use of an offshore EMI or digital treasury card for royalty, vendor, or employee payments outside the regulated banking spine
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion on the EMI's status under the Retail Payment Activities Act and PCMLTFA, sponsoring-bank agreement, FINTRAC money-service-business registration certificate, prescribed list of permitted transaction types, documented prohibition on personal/consumer cash access, monthly reconciliation of EMI settlement to the Canadian bank operating account, and board-approved treasury policy restricting foreign EMI use to non-fiduciary petty purchasing only.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions from non-resident partners must be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the remitting bank to the CA_LP's Schedule I Canadian bank settlement account. The payment should carry the bank's standard business-to-business remittance purpose code, with the remittance information field showing 'Limited partnership capital contribution - CA_LP - no goods or services.' Prior to debiting, the Canadian bank will require executed KYC and source-of-funds documentation; wire pre-notification with a signed contribution resolution, bank reference letter from the remitting bank, and partner registry extract will accelerate clearance. No Investment Canada Act pre-clearance or exchange-control permit is required for a passive capital injection into a BC limited partnership, but all documentary evidence must be retained for FINTRAC and bank suspicious-transaction-reporting requirements. The funds should never be described as trade proceeds, because that would activate trade-monitoring and customs-related review.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For settlement of designer-toy inventory purchases and logistics services, the primary clearing rails are: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier wire payments in USD, EUR, CNY, JPY, or CAD; (ii) ICC UCP600 documentary letters of credit issued or confirmed by a Canadian Schedule I bank for large manufacturing orders; (iii) domestic Canadian-dollar disbursements via the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or bank electronic transfer for local warehouse and BC service providers; (iv) USD clearing via the Canadian bank's US correspondent, typically through CHIPS or Fedwire, for North American suppliers. For mainland China suppliers, USD-CNY conversion is executed bank-side under the Canadian bank's own FX licence; in all cases, settlement must be supported by purchase orders, commercial invoices, bill-of-lading, customs entry, and confirmation that the beneficiary is the actual trading counterparty and not a pass-through collection account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot foreign exchange contracts for operational CAD/USD/CNY/JPY conversion executed with a Schedule I Canadian bank for commercial payment needs.

Customised deliverable FX forwards with a Canadian bank, documented under the International Foreign Exchange Master Agreement (IFEMA) or bank standard paper, limited to genuine forecast exposure arising from inventory procurement, licensing royalties, and e-commerce platform settlements.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or non-deliverable currencies where the bank counterparty is unwilling or unable to effect physical delivery, with settlement in CAD or USD against an agreed fixing rate and a genuine trade-hedging rationale.

Cross-currency swaps between CAD and USD or CNY for medium-term capital and trade-finance restructuring, entered into only with a regulated Canadian bank, subject to bilateral ISDA documentation and Canadian derivatives trade-reporting requirements where applicable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 30 days after the anniversary of registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Financial penalties and timeline triggering administrative strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory independent audit required for limited partnerships unless gross revenue exceeds $1 million or public company status applies

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation of ultimate beneficial owners and partners required upon material changes or transfers

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: N/A (pass-through LP; no entity-level corporate tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: None at entity level; income flows through to partners for personal taxation with possible deductions

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2125 Partnership Return of Income filed electronically via CRA My Business Account or eFILE

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: N/A - Canadian LP; no non-resident filing required
N/A - Canadian LP; no non-resident filing required
N/A - Canadian LP; no non-resident filing required

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty $50 per month or part thereof, maximum $1,000; non-filing penalty $5,000; criminal prosecution possible for evasion

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: N/A - LP distributions are not dividends and are not subject to withholding tax
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: N/A - No dividend withholding tax applies; no DTA or TRC required
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 25% statutory rate, reduced to 0-15% under applicable tax treaties; Royalties: 25% statutory rate, reduced to 0-10% under applicable tax treaties

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: $250,000 CAD (threshold for related-party transactions requiring transfer pricing documentation)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: N/A - Canada has no mandatory Economic Substance Regulations; general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR) and substance requirements apply

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-submission of T2125 by statutory deadline
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: $50 per month penalty (max $1,000); $5,000 non-filing penalty; possible criminal charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: N/A - Limited partnerships provide limited liability; partners liable only for their allocable tax share

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting income, overstating deductions, or false statements
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to $1 million and imprisonment up to 5 years under Income Tax Act; civil penalties also apply
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: N/A - Limited partnerships provide limited liability; partners liable only for their allocable tax share

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or maintain arm's-length transfer pricing documentation or using non-arm's-length pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty up to $500,000 per transaction or 10% of transaction value; possible reassessment and interest charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: N/A - Limited partnerships provide limited liability; partners liable only for their allocable tax share
